ImageDescription.value:
Heiliggrabkapelle, Monastery Endowment of the Holy Grave, Heiligengrabe, Brandenburg, Germany
The Holy Sepulchre Chapel belongs to the Cistercian convent, which was founded in 1287. As early as the 14th century, a “Holy Sepulchre” is mentioned at this location, which gave rise to the name Heiligengrabe (Holy Sepulchre).
The present late Gothic chapel was consecrated in 1512 and built around 1520 on the site of earlier, more modest predecessor buildings.
The building is a four-bay, star-vaulted hall structure made of brick with striking stepped gables. It is considered a masterpiece of North German brick Gothic architecture.

Artist.value: Dietmar Rabich

ImageDescription.value:
50 Pfennig "Notgeld" banknote (emergency money) of Berlin, district Tiergarten (1921), size: 55 mm x 105 mm.
The reverse shows the first German steamboat, the "Prinzessin Charlotte von Preußen", around 1830.
However the date 1830 is mistaken, as the "Charlotte von Preußen" was already dismantled in 1824.
